title: The Web as a System
description: Understand the web as a request/response conversation between browser and server, trace URLs, HTTP status codes, HTML/CSS/JS roles, and inspect real network exchanges.

title: Thinking Like a Programmer
description: Develop the core engineering mindset: decomposing problems into exact steps, tracing state changes, forming falsifiable hypotheses, and isolating bugs systematically.

title: HTML: Structure and Meaning
description: Author semantic, accessible HTML documents from scratch: document trees, headings, landmarks, links, images, lists, tables, and labelled forms.

title: CSS: Make the Structure Visible
description: Master how CSS targets and styles the document tree: selectors, specificity, cascade resolution, box model geometry, typography, color contrast, and visual hierarchy.

title: Layout and Responsive Design
description: Design resilient page layouts using normal flow, Flexbox axes and wrapping, two-dimensional CSS Grid, fluid sizing constraints, and responsive media queries.

title: Accessible Interface Craft
description: Build interfaces usable by everyone: keyboard navigation, focus management, semantic landmarks, accessible names, form error associations, and non-color state signals.

title: JavaScript: The Language of Behavior
description: Write clear, predictable JavaScript logic: values, variables, expressions, functions, conditionals, arrays, objects, iteration, and pure data transformations.

title: JavaScript in the Browser
description: Connect JavaScript to live web pages: querying DOM nodes, handling user events, updating UI state cleanly, preventing default browser actions, and event delegation.

title: TypeScript: Make Intent Explicit
description: Model data and contracts with static types: type annotations, object interfaces, union types, narrowing, discriminated unions, and catching bugs before runtime.

title: Web Data and APIs
description: Coordinate asynchronous network data with fetch(), Promises, async/await, JSON parsing, HTTP status handling, loading/empty/error UI states, and resilient requests.

title: Git, GitHub, and Team Workflow
description: Collaborate safely in engineering teams: atomic commits, working tree inspection, feature branches, pull requests, code review habits, and resolving merge conflicts.

title: React: Think in UI State
description: Shift from manual DOM mutation to declarative UI: components as pure functions of props and state, JSX rendering, list keys, conditional UI, and state derivation.

title: React: Interaction and Effects
description: Handle interactive state transitions and external synchronization: useState updates, controlled forms, immutable state updates, useEffect lifecycles, and cleanup.

title: React: Component Design and Application Patterns
description: Design maintainable component trees: single-responsibility boundaries, lifting state to the lowest common owner, composition with children, and custom hooks.

title: Routing, Data Flow, and React Applications
description: Architect multi-view React applications: URL-driven state, dynamic route parameters, nested layouts, route-level data fetching, and end-to-end feature flows.

title: Next.js Application Engineering
description: Build full-stack web applications with Next.js App Router: file-system routing, Server vs. Client Components, server-side data fetching, mutations, and rendering tradeoffs.

title: Application State
description: Master production state architecture: classifying UI vs. server cache vs. URL state, avoiding redundant derived state, Context boundaries, reducers, and scalable stores.
